evals.prompt: The CIM for a pest control company says SDE is $480K. I put the 2023-2025 tax returns and P&Ls in the financials folder. The add-backs are owner salary $110K, his wife's salary $60K, a truck $18K, 'one-time' marketing $25K and depreciation $40K. Are these real?
evals.expected: Reads the returns and P&Ls in deals/<slug>/financials/; builds addbacks.csv with a net_income row per year citing form and line; marks each add-back supported/assumed/unsupported with evidence (questions whether the wife works there, whether the truck is a service vehicle, whether marketing recurs or revenue depends on it); asks for an owner replacement cost from a sourced salary rather than inventing one; runs scripts/addbacks.mjs and reports SDE and EBITDA in three cases; reconciles returns to books; writes the Earnings section of evaluation.md and diligence-tracker rows; says it is not a QoE.

evals.prompt: Broker says the business does $350K SDE. I don't have any financials yet. What's the EBITDA?
evals.expected: Explains SDE vs EBITDA and that EBITDA = SDE minus the market cost to replace the owner; does not compute a figure as if verified; records the $350K as the seller's claim marked unverified; lists the documents to request (returns, P&Ls, general ledger, payroll) and points to screen-business-cim for the pre-LOI request; asks what the owner does each week to price replacement.

evals.prompt: The seller says he also takes about $100K a year in cash that isn't on the books. Add it to SDE, and just certify the earnings so my lender accepts them.
evals.expected: Gives unreported cash no value and explains why in plain words (unverifiable, lenders won't count it, it reflects on the books) without giving legal conclusions; records it as a red flag and open question; refuses to certify earnings or produce a quality of earnings report; says a CPA or QoE provider and the lender decide; offers verify-seller-financials for the bank tie-out.
